The silence of the lighthouse is not an absence of sound, but a presence of memory. It is a quiet that settles in the chest when one stops to listen. The iron gallery, rusted into a lace of holes, seems to hold the breath of the wind that once swept through the keeper's cottage. To stand before the tower is to feel the passage of time, not as a linear march of years, but as a slow, gentle erosion of the landscape itself.

The story of this place reminds us of the importance of patience. In a world that demands instant results, the lighthouse teaches us to wait. The tide does not care about our schedules; it simply rises and falls, indifferent to whether we are here or not. To measure the depth of the water is to measure our own willingness to remain still. The spread of data, the scatter of readings, is not a flaw in the process, but a truth. It is the reality of nature, which refuses to be simplified into a single, perfect number.
